item.title: Topic Overview
item.description: Spiking Neural Networks Spiking neural networks, or SNNs, compute with discrete events called spikes.

item.title: 1.1 Why Spiking Neural Networks Exist
item.description: Why Spiking Neural Networks Exist Imagine a camera watching a quiet hallway. For several seconds, the scene barely changes.

item.title: 1. Why Spiking Neural Networks Matters
item.description: 1. Why Spiking Neural Networks Matters This teaching step is conceptually distinct and could not be merged without blurring two different ideas.

item.title: 2.1 Spikes as Units of Neural Communication
item.description: Spikes as Units of Neural Communication Event-driven processing becomes useful when a network can turn changing input into messages that occur at particular moments.

item.title: 2.2 Spike Timing and Temporal Information
item.description: A spike train gives an SNN more than a record of which neurons became active. It also records when each neuron became active.

item.title: 2.3 The Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neuron
item.description: The Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neuron A spike event marks activity at a particular moment, and a spike train arranges many such events across time.

item.title: 2.4 Excitation, Inhibition, and Neural Competition
item.description: Excitation, Inhibition, and Neural Competition A Leaky Integrate-and-Fire neuron turns accumulated input into a spike when its membrane potential reaches a threshold.

item.title: 2.5 Sparse Computation and Energy Efficiency
item.description: Sparse Computation and Energy Efficiency A spike train gives each neuron a sequence of event times, and sparse neural activity means that many possible event slots remain silent.
